findings: Both captures describe PaymentMethod as payment instrument details used with PaymentIntent to take payment, or SetupIntent plus Customer to save for future use. The model holds billing and type-specific details, not amount or currency, and the SEPA example is illustrative. Stripe recommends creating PaymentMethods with Stripe.js to handle sensitive data and customer actions. Dashboard activates available methods generally immediately without additional contracts (old 6-17,65-90; new 7-18,70-100).

Customer actions identified by PaymentIntent.next_action include bank redirect to approve, a one-time verification code conveyed to the API, and a customer push of bank funds; the card example excludes 3D Secure. For immediate methods such as cards, the described result is succeeded or requires_payment_method. ACH illustrates delayed status, for which the Intent is processing until the result and the merchant keeps the order pending until payment succeeds (old 19-39; new 20-40).

Reusable methods may be set up during payment or separately, reducing friction and authentication/decline risk. Some bank transfers are single-use, consumed after an attempt and cannot attach to a Customer (old 41-47; new 42-48).

Configure an event destination for action-required or delayed methods and verify webhook signatures to authenticate Stripe as sender. payment_intent.processing means submitted for a delayed method and wait, payment_intent.succeeded means fulfill, and payment_intent.payment_failed means ask for another method. Alternatives remain low-volume Dashboard tracking, lower-reliability rate-limited polling, or partner application (old 49-63; new 50-68). Events and buyer action preserve the payment-status boundary, with succeeded meaning processing-flow completion rather than irrevocable funds.

Keep the existing link to wiki/sources/source-stripe-payment-intents.md (source 67-70) and connect the Payment Methods API overview reciprocally with wiki/concepts/stripe-payment-methods.md:76-103 for method roles and wiki/concepts/stripe-payment-intents.md:77-96,140-158 for lifecycle, Charge outcomes and status handling. Stripe index 21 and 729-730 and root index 7 already provide entry routes. Keep the distinct supported-methods overview source in the payment-methods concept.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-payment-methods-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-payment-methods-api-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-payment-methods.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods, a PaymentMethod contains payment instrument details, including billing details and a type-specific hash. A PaymentIntent takes payment, while a SetupIntent and Customer save details for later use. The buyer takes any bank approval, one-time-code, or push-funds action indicated by PaymentIntent.next_action. Cards illustrate immediate succeeded or requires_payment_method outcomes, while ACH debit illustrates processing with the merchant holding the order pending. A verified succeeded webhook supports fulfillment, and failed prompts the merchant to request another method (old raw lines 8-63; new raw lines 9-68). November defines succeeded as completed processing with possible later refund, dispute, return, or reversal. source-stripe-payment-methods.md reflects the earlier roles but must replace the guaranteed-funds language and distinguish merchant order status from Intent status.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods, the substantive November 7 change is the explicit removal of the April 19 guaranteed-funds wording in favor of successful method processing with later refunds, disputes, returns or reversals possible. November also expressly recommends pending-order handling and webhook-signature verification (old raw lines 33-39 and old raw lines 49-57; new raw lines 34-40 and new raw lines 50-60). The new event-destination URL, title and table formatting, separated tracking subsection, and reformatted SEPA example are navigation or representation, with the event semantics and PaymentMethod field roles preserved. Keep the April authority dated in source-stripe-payment-methods.md, distinguish later Charge outcomes from the succeeded Intent, and make methods and Intent lifecycle routes reciprocal without replacing the separate regional-methods overview (old raw lines 59-95; new raw lines 62-105).
